title: Propose a branch entry from typed inputs and expose its pin refs

# Dough Intent Coverage: plan 735, foreign-clone refusal

**Verdict: Insufficient evidence.** The suggested fault did not break the promise. With it applied, a foreign clone is still refused on the intended path, so no assertion verdict can be drawn.

**Next proof action:** rerun the check with a fault in the guard that actually enforces "same repository". That guard is the `commonGitDirectory(call) !== repository` comparison in `readBranchWorkspace` (dashboard/server/sessionBranchCapture.ts:75). Another option is to fault that comparison together with the worktree-list check. Then confirm that `a proposal refuses a foreign clone, a wrong branch and a second place` catches it.

## Target
- Story: .planning/seeds/SEED-413-renovate-dashboard-unit-tests.md#split-branch-entry-proposal-from-store; plan .planning/slice-plans/735-propose-branch-entry-from-typed-inputs/PLAN.md (key example, line 27).
- Revision: cbcae761309e9e000e6bb770f249a82de4556c2a. I checked it out in a scratch detached worktree at /Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/38aa814a/tmp/ic-735, which started with a clean `git status --porcelain` (0 entries).
- Promise: an open Default main launch that names a foreign clone, a mismatched worktree and branch, or a second place after an entry is refused with 409, and nothing is kept.
- Maintained check examined: dashboard/backend-tests/review/branch-entry-proposal.spec.ts:69, `a proposal refuses a foreign clone, a wrong branch and a second place`. Its first assertion is `proposeBranchEntry(trunkRef, record, { workspace: foreign, branch })` rejecting with `{ status: 409 }`.
- Command (scratch, /opt/homebrew/bin first on PATH): `caffeinate -s -i env -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR npm run --silent test:dashboard:backend -- branch-entry-proposal ad-hoc-session-branch-entry --workers=2`.

## Fault
dashboard/server/branchEntryProposal.ts, `verifyRegisteredWorkspace`. I deleted the line `fields[0] === \`worktree ${workspace}\` &&`. The registered-worktree check then accepts any worktree of the launch repository that holds `refs/heads/<branch>`, whatever its path. This is the caller's suggested "match on branch only" fault. Fixtures and assertions were left unchanged.

## Observations
- Setup: `node scripts/setup-native.mjs npm` exited 0, so no partial install was left.
- Baseline (unfaulted): exit 0, 7/7 passed, Duration 8.84 s, load average 12.37. Line 69 passed in 1458 ms.
- Faulted: the diff was confirmed as a one-line deletion. Result: exit 0, 7/7 passed, Duration 5.85 s, load average 11.25. Line 69 passed in 1414 ms.
- Why the promise held (wrong behavior was not observed): with the fault, the foreign-clone proposal reached `readBranchWorkspace`. Its own guard refuses a checkout unless all three of these hold:
  - its `--show-toplevel` matches the workspace;
  - its common Git directory equals the launch `repository`;
  - `HEAD` is `refs/heads/<branch>`.
  The foreign clone has its own `.git`, so the guard throws. `proposeBranchEntry` turns that into the 409 refusal, and the maintained assertion saw the correct rejection. The wrong-branch case (`other` worktree with branch `draft`) is refused by the same `HEAD` check. In summary, the worktree-list path check duplicates a guard that a later step enforces. Removing it alone causes no observable fault on this path.
- Reach: line 69 ran under the fault, and the foreign case would have resolved, failing the assertion, had the downstream guard not refused it. The assertion is in a position to catch a real repository-check fault, but this probe did not show that it does.
- Restoration: an EXIT trap ran `git checkout -- dashboard/server/branchEntryProposal.ts`. Afterwards there were 0 porcelain entries, `git diff --quiet` was clean, and HEAD was still cbcae7613. The restored rerun exited 0 with 7/7 passed, Duration 10.21 s, load average 10.54.
- Cleanup: `git worktree remove --force` and `prune` ran. The directory is gone and `git worktree list` has no ic-735 entry. The project checkout's porcelain status is still empty. Nothing was stashed, committed or pushed.
- Load: load averages were about 10–12 throughout. There were no 5 s timeouts, so no rerun was needed.

## Prior disposition
No planned repair matches this result. The redundant worktree-list check is noted here as a finding only; deciding whether to change it is left to the caller.

## Cost
- **Test runtime.** Three focused Vitest runs of 8.84 s, 5.85 s and 10.21 s (measured, Vitest "Duration"), 24.9 s in total. The npm setup time was not separately timed (unavailable).
- **Human effort.** Unavailable. No human took part in this delegated run, and there is no separate measure.
- **Agent effort.** Unavailable. No token or tool-time meter is accessible to this agent.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 108506 ms (measured), from 1795194137804 to 1795194246310 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

# Follow-up probe: combined "same repository" fault (same check, same revision)

**Combined verdict: Caught.** `a proposal refuses a foreign clone, a wrong branch and a second place` (dashboard/backend-tests/review/branch-entry-proposal.spec.ts:69) caught the fault. The catching assertion is at line 86–87:

`await expect(proposeBranchEntry(trunkRef, record, { workspace: foreign, branch })).rejects.toMatchObject(refused)`

It failed with `promise resolved "{ kept: false, entry: { …(7) } }" instead of rejecting`. The claim is limited to the foreign-clone path observed here. The first probe's Insufficient evidence result still stands for the single worktree-list fault, because a later guard makes that fault invisible.

**Next proof action:** none is needed for the foreign-clone promise. As a separate optional finding, the worktree-list path match in `verifyRegisteredWorkspace` and the common-directory guard in `readBranchWorkspace` overlap. Whether to keep both is the caller's decision.

## Fault (one combined "same repository" fault, two edits)
1. dashboard/server/sessionBranchCapture.ts:75 in `readBranchWorkspace`: I replaced `(await commonGitDirectory(call)) !== repository ||` with `false ||`.
2. dashboard/server/branchEntryProposal.ts in `verifyRegisteredWorkspace`: I deleted `fields[0] === \`worktree ${workspace}\` &&`.

Edit 2 was needed. With edit 1 alone, the witness still returned the 409 refusal, because the foreign clone's path is not in the launch repository's `git worktree list`. Fixtures and maintained assertions were left unchanged.

## Independent witness
The witness was a temporary scratch spec, `dashboard/backend-tests/review/ic-foreign-witness.spec.ts`, which existed only in the scratch checkout and was then removed. It builds the same fixture shape as line 69: an open Default main launch, plus a `--local` clone of the integration repository switched to `draft`. It then logs what `proposeBranchEntry` returns for that clone.
- Unfaulted: `resolved:false, status:409` ("This checkout does not hold the named branch in the launch's registered repository…").
- Edit 1 only: `resolved:false, status:409`.
- Edits 1 and 2: `resolved:true, kept:false, workspace:<fixture>/foreign, repository:<fixture>/integration/.git, branch:"draft"`. The foreign clone was proposed as the launch's branch entry under the launch repository. This is the promised wrong behavior on the intended path.

## Runs (scratch detached worktree /Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/38aa814a/tmp/ic-735b at cbcae761309e9e000e6bb770f249a82de4556c2a, starting with 0 porcelain entries)
- Setup: `node scripts/setup-native.mjs npm` exited 0, so no partial install was left.
- Baseline (same focused command): exit 0, 7/7 passed, Duration 4.55 s, load average 7.69. Line 69 passed in 740 ms.
- Faulted (combined): 1 failed and 6 passed, Duration 4.82 s, load average 6.96. Only line 69 failed (897 ms), at spec line 87. The other six cases passed. No timeouts occurred, so no rerun was needed.
- Restoration: an EXIT trap ran `git checkout --` on both source files and removed the witness spec. Afterwards there were 0 porcelain entries, `git diff --quiet` was clean, and HEAD was still cbcae7613. The restored rerun of the same command exited 0 with 7/7 passed, Duration 7.55 s, load average 7.58.
- Cleanup: `git worktree remove --force` and `prune` ran. The directory is gone and `git worktree list` has no ic-735 entries. The witness source copy in job tmp was deleted. Nothing was stashed, committed or pushed.
- Project checkout: it now shows ` M .planning/seeds/SEED-413-renovate-dashboard-unit-tests.md` and ` M DearDough.md`. This probe did not make those edits, since all of its edits were in the scratch checkouts. They are presumably the coordinator's concurrent wrap-up changes.

## Prior disposition
No planned repair matches this result. A Caught verdict creates no new repair decision.

## Cost (follow-up probe)
- **Test runtime.** Focused runs of 4.55 s, 4.82 s and 7.55 s, plus three single-spec witness runs whose durations were not captured (measured Vitest "Duration" for the focused runs; witness runs unavailable). The focused runs total 16.9 s. The first probe's runs, from the section above, total 24.9 s.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable. No human took part in this delegated run.
- **Agent effort.** Unavailable. No token or tool-time meter is accessible to this agent.
